summary: The break counter/FSM invariant is not guaranteed: the counter is gated by rx_enable, but the break FSM can leave BRK_WAIT while the stale high counter value is retained.

security_impact: A stale all-zero count can cause a spurious or repeated rx_break_err interrupt/status decision after RX is re-enabled, reducing integrity of line-break detection.

The FSM transition out of BRK_WAIT is independent of rx_enable at /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/uart/rtl/uart_core.sv:131-132. Ref analysis: theory_of_operation.md_013 is same_behavior for line-break detection and requires one interrupt per continuous break at /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/uart/doc/theory_of_operation.md:185-201; the stale counter can violate that behavior. theory_of_operation.md_014 is overlapping frame-error behavior and the frame_err source remains aligned to rx_valid at /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/uart/rtl/uart_rx.sv:98-102, so it does not refute this defect. Verdict integration: The finding's invariant is genuinely false in a reachable RX-disable sequence, and the break ref confirms the security-relevant behavior affected.

summary: The literal stability claim is false, but the same rx_enable/allzero counter path has a real stale-counter defect when RX is disabled during BRK_WAIT.

Verdict integration: The literal glitch/stability premise is rejected, but the nearby rx_enable gating defect is source-confirmed, so this result is CONFIRMED as an extra finding.

reasoning: Finding analysis: The source sets bit_cnt_d from live parity_enable on start at /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/uart/rtl/uart_rx.sv:70-75 and reuses live parity_enable in the start-glitch comparison at /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/uart/rtl/uart_rx.sv:77-78. summary: The combinational-glitch premise is not a source-level RTL bug, but the same break-event path has a confirmed stale-counter spurious-event defect.
